verdict: Home Depot grew sales 4.8% to $41.8B as bigger tickets offset fewer trips, but profit slipped 4% to $3.3B because the cost of merchandise rose faster than sales.

kpis.label: Comparable sales
kpis.note: +0.4% in the U.S.; currency added ~0.55 points

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold through 2,361 Home Depot stores and its website, plus over 1,280 SRS locations — the professional-supply business Home Depot has been buying to win more contractor spending.

flow.costPlain: What Home Depot paid suppliers for the merchandise it sold, plus the cost of getting it into stores.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Store payroll, rent, advertising and running the head office.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of stores, warehouses and equipment over their useful lives — including $171M of amortization tied to acquired companies like SRS.

otherDetail: Interest and other, net was a $604M cost: $611M of interest expense on Home Depot's debt, partly offset by $7M of interest and other income.
follow100Note: Two-thirds of every $100 goes straight back out as the cost of the merchandise itself — retail keeps a much thinner slice than software does. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Demand is flat, not falling
takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 0.6% (0.4% in the U.S.), with currency adding about half a point. Management said underlying demand looked much as it did through fiscal 2025, despite consumer uncertainty and housing affordability pressure.

takeaways.title: Bigger baskets, fewer trips
takeaways.text: The average ticket rose 2.3% to $92.76 while customer transactions fell 0.9% to 391.1 million (excluding HD Supply and SRS). Shoppers came less often but spent more each visit.

takeaways.title: Margins got squeezed
takeaways.text: Cost of sales rose 6.0% against sales growth of 4.8%, so gross profit grew only 2.4% and the gross margin narrowed to 33.0% from 33.8% a year ago. Operating income fell 3% to $4,981M.

oneTimers: Adjusted results exclude $171M of amortization from acquired intangibles (including $119M tied to SRS) — on that basis EPS was $3.43 instead of the GAAP $3.30.
Home Depot reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 guidance with this print: sales growth of about 2.5–4.5%, comparable sales roughly flat to +2%, and a gross margin near 33.1%.
